label: Prefill GEMM BLOCK_M
mechanism: prefill-scale grouped NVFP4 GEMM calls take BLOCK_M 32, halving the per-expert in-register dequant that is 93% of prefill CUDA time
hypothesis: The bench runs in lockstep cohorts (osl_cap=128 exactly, ledger gen_tokens/requests = 128.0 on every row -> all 64 co-residents retire together and 64 replacement prefills serialize), so cycle = 64 x 1.92 s prefill + 128 x step: this model reproduces exp-0006's 21.5 (step 2.01) and exp-0008's accepted 45.3 (180.8 s cycle, prefill term 122.9 s = 68%). Profiling the per-seq prefill on the resident model (torch.profiler, T=574, /workspace/logs/t_prefill_profile_exp0009_2026-07-30.log) shows it is NOT dispatch-bound: 93.4% of prefill CUDA time is the exp-0003 grouped packed-NVFP4 GEMM (_gate_up_silu 16.0 ms + _down_scale 5.9 ms of each 24.3 ms MoE layer; attention 1.1 ms), whose kernels re-dequantize the full weight tile per (expert, n-tile, k-chunk, M-CHUNK) — cost = ceil(rows_per_expert/BLOCK_M) full-matrix ALU dequants per hit expert, and at prefill (~all 256 experts hit, 17-24 rows each) BLOCK_M 16 pays it twice. This diff (one conditional in moe_experts_packed + constants): calls with pair count P >= 2048 (T >= 342 — every prefill; unreachable by decode, B<=256 -> P<=1536) launch with BLOCKS (32,128,128); decode-scale calls keep the exp-0003 specialization BIT-IDENTICALLY, so the headline decode step is untouched. Measured: config sweep on synthetic checkpoint-shape packs (10 reps, t_moe_config_sweep2 log) T=736 19.9 -> 13.5 ms, T=1018 25.0 -> 14.0 ms (BLOCK_M 64 is an sm_103a LLVM crash; (32,128,128) w4 s3 best of 8 configs); resident-model e2e walk T=574 1.49 -> 0.94 s, T=1018 2.6-est -> 1.55 s, serial 8-cohort slice 18.45 -> 9.79 s (1.7-1.9x warm).
predicted_delta: +30-45% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s (45.3 -> ~59-66; cycle model 8192/(64 x P1 + 57.9 s decode residual) with in-situ mean prefill P1 1.92 s -> ~1.02-1.17 s gives 61-67, floored to 59 for serve-path glue that does not shrink; prefill_heavy should gain a similar factor on its own row when next measured — the same kernels dominate at ISL 8K)
